purpose: Establish the FIRST live combat state for a new episode/scenario, from a hand-authored or reconstructed spec (Common/schemas/combat_scenario_input_schema.json)
input_state_origin: scenario_spec (spec dict passed by the caller - CombatEnv.reset()/preflight_validate()/generate_heuristic_trajectories.generate_trajectory()/probe_*.py)
call_frequency: 1 per episode (CombatEnv.reset() / preflight_validate() call this exactly once each; every online-eval/teacher-gen script calls preflight_validate() then CombatEnv.adopt_state(), which does NOT call initialize() again - see combat_env.py:95-106)
assumed_side_effects: Sets engine turnNumber to 1 unconditionally (module docstring: 'turnNumber always resets to 1 under ResetFromScenario... verified experimentally'); establishes enemy_max_hp baseline the wrapper tracks in Python thereafter
api_used_after: game.GetObservation() implicitly via ResetResult.Observation; caller then uses the SAME shared GameInstance for every subsequent Step()/GetLegalActions() until the next restore
game_instance_lifetime: Shared singleton (emulator_bridge.shared_game_instance()) - lives for the whole OS process, reused (via repeated Reset) across every episode/decision, never disposed by this codebase

purpose: Rebuild a live combat state from a PREVIOUSLY-CAPTURED Python-side engine_state snapshot (a mid-combat resume point), immediately before either (a) a fresh GetLegalActions() call or (b) applying one more action
input_state_origin: battle_state.engine_state (the caller's own snapshot - see call sites below for who holds it)
combat_start_or_mid_state: mid_state (every call except the very first initialize() of an episode)
call_frequency: Called from 2 places, each potentially many times per decision - see below
assumed_side_effects: Discards ResetFromScenario's own returned LegalActions (never reads reset_result.LegalActions - see known_risks.md for this as a redundant-call observation); resets engine turnNumber to 1 again (same mechanism as initialize()) EVERY time
api_used_after: game.GetLegalActions() (enumerate_legal_actions path) or game.Step()+continuation loop (apply_action path), both immediately after, on the SAME game object returned by _restore()
game_instance_lifetime: Same shared singleton - _restore() calls ResetFromScenario on it again
column10: effectively discarding whatever combat state the engine held before this call and replacing it wholesale

purpose: Get a fresh, authoritative legal-action list for a NON-ActionContinuation state - code comment explains this is preferred over any cached list because 'StepResult.LegalActions after a complex card play is stale' in some observed cases
input_state_origin: battle_state passed in by the caller (CombatEnv.get_legal_actions() / HeuristicAgent.choose_action_with_detail() / HeuristicAgent's own per-candidate loop indirectly via apply_action / preflight_validate())
call_frequency: Once per enumerate_legal_actions() call whenever the state is NOT ActionContinuation-pending (i.e. essentially every top-level decision point) - see call_count_summary.csv for per-decision totals
api_used_after: game.GetLegalActions() called immediately after on the same restored game

purpose: Rebuild the live state immediately before committing (or hypothetically trying, for HeuristicAgent's candidate scoring) one action via Step()
input_state_origin: battle_state passed in by the caller (CombatEnv.step() for the real committed action; HeuristicAgent.choose_action_with_detail()'s per-(action,target)-candidate loop for HYPOTHETICAL, uncommitted scoring restores)
call_frequency: Once per apply_action() call UNLESS live_game is supplied (only true for continuation-loop internal Step()s, which reuse the game object step_live_action() already has - see apply_action()'s own live_game param and its while-loop at battle_emulator.py:901-909, which never re-restores)
game_instance_lifetime: then the ActionContinuation while-loop (same game object
column10: no further restore) if the played action triggers one

input_state_origin: standalone diagnostic scripts from a PAST incident investigation ('emulator_hang' - a prior hang/timeout issue unrelated to this task's no_legal_actions case)
combat_start_or_mid_state: Locally constructed scenario objects inside each script, not the live pipeline's engine_state
call_frequency: combat_start (each script builds its own fresh scenario)
assumed_side_effects: Not part of any currently-invoked pipeline - these are archived one-off repro scripts, not called by battle_emulator.py/combat_env.py/any online_eval script
api_used_after: Same ResetFromScenario semantics as above, but isolated per-script GameInstance
game_instance_lifetime: game.GetLegalActions()/Step() within each standalone script only
column10: Not the shared singleton necessarily - each script constructs its own GameInstance() directly (not verified here to confirm process-per-script isolation, out of this task's scope); kept only as historical evidence/template, not live code
